property_summary: For any admissible newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) as the current owner sets owner to exactly newOwner; the mutant always sets owner to address(0), which differs whenever newOwner != address(0).

Ownership-gated actions require the immediate caller (msg.sender) to be the owner, so a transferOwnership relayed through an intermediary contract always reverts in the reference C; the tx.origin mutant accepts such relayed calls, letting a non-owner contract change owner.
Calling owned() must not change ownership: for any caller address, c.owner() remains address(0) after owned(); the mutant transfers ownership to msg.sender, breaking this for any nonzero caller.

For any non-zero caller who is not the owner, calling owned() must not succeed nor change ownership: the call reverts and owner() stays address(0); the buggy version lets owned() transfer ownership to the caller, so owner() becomes the caller for some fuzzed caller.

For any admissible account, a successful call to owned() must leave the owner unchanged (owned() has no ownership side-effect), but the mutant makes owned() rewrite owner to msg.sender, so for a caller whose resulting owner value can be observed to change the rule is violated.
